title: KeyBanc downgrades Workday, sees limited near-term AI contribution
key_facts: Barchart, 16 Oct: Workday shares slipped on Friday after KeyBanc analyst Jason Celino downgraded the enterprise software company to Sector Weight.
Celino said enthusiasm at Workday Rising does not show when new AI products will lift revenue; KeyBanc sees 'insufficient evidence' of a near-term acceleration.
KeyBanc acknowledged Workday's AI investments could eventually help it beat its reiterated fiscal 2028 targets.
Celino also believes human resources IT budgets could get lower priority as businesses fund more immediate AI initiatives.
Workday stock is about 68% above its late-June price and slipped through its 50-day moving average.
Barchart's consensus rating on Workday is Moderate Buy, with a mean price target of about $208.
quote_evidence: Workday (WDAY) shares are slipping on Friday after KeyBanc questioned how quickly the firm's artificial intelligence (AI) investments would deliver meaningful revenue.
Analyst Jason Celino downgraded the enterprise software company to "Sector Weight."
All in all, KeyBanc's downgrade of Workday shares reflects "insufficient evidence" of a near-term acceleration, even as it recognizes the technology's longer-term potential.
why_it_matters_hint: One analyst doubts AI will lift business software sales soon, even as the shares have run up.
